settings.title: Hair-wash day after a lash appointment is a balancing act
settings.text:
• The head tilt. Leaning back, one hand over your eyes, shampoo running everywhere.
  • Skipping the wash. Dry shampoo for two days so the new set stays perfect.
  • The mascara streaks. Did your makeup, need a quick rinse, now you're starting over.

settings.title: How it works
settings.step1_text: Peel the strip and press it across your forehead, just above the brows. The clear shield hangs in front of your eyes.
settings.step2_text: Tip your head back, lather and rinse. Water and foam slide down the front of the shield.
settings.step3_text: Each shield is single-use, so every shower starts with a clean one.

settings.title: For the first days after your lash appointment
settings.text:
Most lash artists ask you to keep a fresh lash lift or set of extensions dry for the first 24 to 48 hours. The shield lets you wash your hair in that window without the head tilt.

Always follow your own lash artist's aftercare advice.

settings.title: Already did your makeup? Wash your hair anyway
settings.text: Gym after work, a last-minute hair wash before dinner, a morning when the mascara is already on. Stick on a shield, rinse, peel it off and go.

settings.title: Good to know before you buy
settings.text:
• Single-use. The adhesive is made for one shower. Use a fresh shield each time.
  • It keeps spray off the front of your face. It is not a swim mask and does not seal around your eyes, so don't dunk your face under water.
  • Sensitive skin? Try one shield on your inner arm first. Don't stick it on broken or irritated skin.
  • Not for children.
  • Your lash artist's aftercare advice always comes first.
